title: Nebraska Governor Jim Pillen visits Norfolk, recognizes Korean War veterans for their service - NewsBreak
text:
By Alex Prieto-Rivero ,
1 hours ago
NORFOLK , Neb. ( KCAU ) — It was a packed room inside the Norfolk Veterans Home where Nebraska Governor Jim Pillen appeared to recognize Korean War Veterans in honor of America 250.
“I call it an extraordinary goose bump moment,” said Pillen.
14 veterans were recognized for their service during the Korean War, defending a country they had never known.
“I think it’s important we hear the stories of what the greatest generations did,” said Pillen. “Same goes for Vietnam veterans that we’ve been recognizing across the state with pinnings. Freedom takes a lot; it’s not free.”
Story continues below
After each veteran was presented with their coin, some shared stories of their service.
“In Korea, I was in the mountains,” said Korean War Veteran Fred Kappler. “I got stuck up there for 14 weeks in a trench that the Chinese had dug, and the army guys kicked the Chinese outta there… I froze my feet, froze my hands, [and] lost my hearing.”
“I was with the 8th Cavalry Division in Japan,” said Korean War Veteran Harry Brock. “We were up in Hokkaido. Very, very cold.”
Each veteran expressed their gratitude for the governor’s presentation.
“I was really looking forward to this,” said Korean War Veteran Delano Cunningham. “It’s kind of neat!”
Nebraska will host a ceremony to recognize Korean War veterans and present additional challenge coins in person at the Nebraska State Capitol on July 24.
